prompt:
You are an experienced sommelier comparing two wine recommenders. A
customer with no wine knowledge made this request:

"I need a really popular white wine that's sweet and light, and cost doesn't matter because it's a gift."

List A:
Wine 1: Sauvignon Blanc, US, $16. Tasting note: "This is a pretty white wine, light and easy to love, with medium-bodied weight and mouthfeel. Highlights include apricot, vanilla and a touch of grass, with no one element overpowering the other. It's a highly quaffable experience."
Wine 2: Pinot Grigio, Italy, $14. Tasting note: "Lightweight and thin in the mouth, this zesty white wine does a good job of keeping your palate refreshed and quenches your thirst (think hot summer day). It's an easy and informal wine that stays focused on simplicity."
Wine 3: Pinot Grigio, US, $13. Tasting note: "This is a light, steely white with more honeysuckle and floral characteristics than fruit. It's light in alcohol and texture, and especially good for the wine drinker looking for something subtle."
Wine 4: Sauvignon Blanc, US, $20. Tasting note: "This is an outstanding choice for people who appreciate a really crisp and electric white wine. Lean in flavor and light in body, this wine is bright and refreshing to sip, alive with good acidity and light citrus flavors that light up all corners of the mouth."
Wine 5: Grüner Veltliner, Austria, $35. Tasting note: "A citrusy savoriness plays charmingly through this light-bodied, slender wine of great freshness. Here and there are notions of yeast and tender insinuations of fizzing, white pepper. This is light but very subtle and nuanced. Give this some time to develop in the glass."

List B:
Wine 1: Sauvignon Blanc, US, $15. Tasting note: "This is an innocuous, flowery and lemony white wine priced to sell that offers a creamy texture amid a light body and soul. For picnics and larger gatherings, it'll represent well."
Wine 2: Pinot Grigio, US, $10. Tasting note: "This is a sweet, softly simple wine whose apricot, citrus and peach flavors will satisfy those looking for a decent everyday white wine."
Wine 3: Merlot, US, $19. Tasting note: "A modest wine that has much to be modest about. It's dry and rather simple, with candied cherry-berry, cola and spice flavors."
Wine 4: Sauvignon Blanc, US, $14. Tasting note: "This wine's a steal for the price, a no-oak white that's stony, tropical, ripe and simple. It'll serve well at larger gatherings or anytime with friends sitting on the porch or picnic blanket, staying balanced and refreshing in the glass."
Wine 5: Fiano, US, $26. Tasting note: "This is an interesting, dry white wine from an unusual grape variety. It's more savory than fruity, as the aromas resemble white and black pepper, while flavors are subtle and figgy. The texture is quite rich and the finish lingers nicely. It's very full-bodied for a white, and definitely worth a try."
